summary: Iteration-61 backend testing of inter-character communication behaviors on AI characters: (1) RELAY WITH REPLY-BACK, (2) OVERHEAR DURING A CALL (multi-voice segments), (3) PASS THE PHONE (handoff), plus 2 regressions. 5/5 pytest cases PASS on the live preview backend against founder/semidiepie. ElevenLabs voices Rachel/Bella are valid on this account — audio bytes are actually returned (not null) for handoff greeting_audio and all 5 overhear segments. _maybe_relay_to_relative + _relative_pings_user background task runs and completes well inside the 90s polling budget.

backend_tests_detail.TestRelayReplyBack::test_relay_creates_c: PASS — POST /api/ai-characters/A/send {text:'tell your mom I love her'} returns 200 {pending:true}. Background _maybe_relay_to_relative populated db.ai_char_convos (pair_key = sorted(A.id|B.id)) AND B's GET /thread grew by one ai-role message with non-empty text within 90s poll budget.
backend_tests_detail.TestOverhear::test_voice_turn_overhear_r: PASS — POST /voice-turn {text:'can you ask your mom what is for dinner'} returned 200 with 5 segments, each having (audio_url, distant:bool, text:str). Observed interleave A/B/A/B/A → distant=[False,True,False,True,False]; both distant=true and distant=false segments present. 'reply' = closing A line ('Okay Sam, she says pasta sounds good…'). ai_char_convos grew (between-them lines persisted). All segments returned real audio bytes (data:audio/mpeg;base64, ~>50KB each).
backend_tests_detail.TestPassThePhone::test_voice_turn_pass_t: PASS — POST /voice-turn {text:'pass the phone to your mom'} returned 200 with handoff.character_id==B.id, handoff.name==B.name, avatar_url present, greeting_text non-empty ('Hey! It\'s <B first-name>…'), greeting_audio = data URI (~151KB). audio_url = A's hand-off line (~59KB). No 'segments' key (correctly mutually exclusive).
backend_tests_detail.TestRegressionPlainVoiceTurn::test_norma: PASS — POST /voice-turn {text:'how was your day?'} returned 200 {reply, audio_url} with NO 'segments' and NO 'handoff'. Normal single-voice path intact.
backend_tests_detail.TestRegressionRelativeMentionNoIntent::t: PASS — POST /voice-turn {text:'I miss your mom'} matches a relative via _match_relative but neither _wants_passphone nor _wants_relay fires, so route falls through to the normal reply. No 'segments', no 'handoff'. Gating via _wants_passphone/_wants_relay works.

critical_code_review_comments: ai_characters.py is now 2038 lines — still well past the 700-line guideline. The new inter-character block inside voice_turn (lines 1263-1310) is a prime candidate to extract into a helpers module alongside _exchange_lines/_maybe_relay_to_relative.

voice_turn handoff path (lines 1268-1282) calls _tts twice sequentially (hand-off line, then B's greeting). On a slow ElevenLabs these two awaits add up — consider asyncio.gather to parallelise them to cut end-user latency in a live call.

The handoff.greeting_text template is hardcoded to "Hey! It's {rc['name'].split()[0]}. So good to hear your voice." — a bit robotic and doesn't vary. Consider letting the relative character actually generate a short in-persona greeting via _gen_message (same as _relative_pings_user) so it matches their persona.

_wants_relay keyword list contains 'ask my' which is a user-POV phrase ("ask my mom"). On an AI-character thread the user is talking TO the character, so 'ask YOUR mom' is correct and 'ask MY mom' would never semantically apply to the character's relatives — minor dead-code smell.

_maybe_relay_to_relative uses a bare `low = user_text.lower()` pre-filter list (lines 831) that includes 'know' — this will match the word 'know' anywhere (e.g. 'I don't know what to do') and then still require a relation-token match, so it's not a bug but the pre-filter is nearly a no-op. A tighter word-boundary check would be clearer.

voice_turn pass-the-phone branch stores only A's hand-off line via _store but does NOT store B's greeting in B's thread. If the client crashes mid-call after handoff, the greeting the user heard is never in B's chat history. Consider _store(rc['id'], ..., 'ai', greet).

Overhear path persists convo lines (lines[:-1]) and stores lines[-1] in A's thread, but does not store any part of the exchange in B's thread. If parity matters for B's unread/last_message, nothing shows up there.
test_credentials: founder email login (/api/auth/login): semidiepie@gmail.com / Semi123! (used because the test runs non-interactively and needs is_super_admin). PIN login is also available.
seed_data_creation: Per test module: 2 TEST_-prefixed ai-characters (TEST_Alice_* with Rachel voice 21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM, TEST_Barbara_* with Bella voice EXAVITQu4vr4xnSDxMaL) with mutual mother/daughter relationships and your_name='Sam'. Teardown deletes both characters via DELETE /api/ai-characters/{id}, then prunes ai_char_convos (pair_key), ai_char_state and ai_char_messages for those two ids directly via pymongo. The user's real characters (Hope, Amara, Juliette, Nova, Sage AI) are NOT touched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_iteration61_inter_character.py -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/iteration61_inter_char.xml  (~30s). The test uses pymongo directly against MONGO_URL/DB_NAME to verify ai_char_convos (there's no public API for that collection). TTS is working on this account for both premade voices — if it ever starts returning null bytes, assertions already allow audio_url to be None; only structural keys are asserted. The 90s poll budget for the relay path is generous — in practice it completed well under 30s. ElevenLabs quota: this suite runs ~8 TTS calls total (handoff: 2, overhear: 5, plus relative_pings_user: 0 — it's text only).
rca of the issue: N/A — all three new behaviors (pass-the-phone handoff, overhear segments, relay reply-back) work end-to-end on the live preview backend and the two regression paths still work. The two gating helpers (_wants_passphone / _wants_relay) correctly distinguish 'pass the phone to your mom' / 'ask your mom …' from a passive mention like 'I miss your mom'.
